_doc: credit-verify-outbound.sh CAPACITY caps (Fable 10-30 23:4xZ: the fixed small daily caps go; the safety is the auto-kill: bounce / spam / unsub > 2 %, any fraud hit, the zero-read, v1's 2 h sample). daily_cap = users messaged per campaign per UTC day by segment (credit: the runner's own segment record; claim: ledger rows of the campaign). shared_daily_cap = every campaign of the group together per UTC day (m2's shared send CEILINGS inside notify: credit 2,500 / claim 500; messaging-monitoring-m2, H-DevOps #4598 - this file's claim cap is the live 200, inside that ceiling). A campaign with no row or no group never applies (fail closed). Raising a cap is a PR. holds = the Gmail-side DATED WINDOWS [key=dated-windows-are-data] (l1 ruling 2026-11-02, ruling-o-retire-1102.md): a code literal with a date in it is a CI red with a countdown on it. holds.gmail is the /o promise clause (an extra sentence in a uvn-status ask) and the hold on gmail-vouched users: clause_open=false retires it, due_at closes it on the clock. The gate re-reads this file on every run, so closing needs no deploy. Reviewed baseline: deploy overwrites - 2026-11-13 (verif-reask-14d-r1): node-8 holds a copy of this file edited in place (sha256 4321089f93b3a4422925f468e794bd4ef7c7395b6ba7587d133e9d2b4e5fb3d9, mtime 2026-11-13T07:01Z, read 18:22Z and again 22:26Z), which the deploy's delta gate would otherwise stop on. Repo aligned to the live node-8 values - these are NOT new decisions, they are the values node-8 already runs, carried so the deploy changes none of them: daily_cap.uvn-status paid/free 2500/2500 -> 2000/2000; daily_cap.proof-need-ask paid/free 2500/2500 -> 400/400; shared_daily_cap.claim 500 -> 25; tick_cap.uvn-status {free: 60} -> {paid: 50, free: 50}; and the rows absent from the repo copy and live on node-8: tick_cap.proof-need-ask {paid: 50, free: 5}, tick_cap.claim-proof-ask {paid: 25, free: 25}, and the four armed_families rows (uvn-status 2026-10-31T18:02Z, status-doc-received 2026-11-03T12:56Z, claim-proof-ask 2026-11-03T18:58Z, proof-need-ask 2026-11-10T02:17Z) with their live unsigned_from values. Nothing is raised. That copy is also written outside a deploy (an operator's edit; the node-8 watchdog that sets tick_cap.uvn-status to 0/0 on a hard stop), and with the marker above a deploy writes this file over whatever is there: compare the live copy with this one before deploying a change to it. The only additions are the uvn-reminder-14 rows (captain 2026-11-13 15:08Z: one reminder to a verification non-responder after 14 days; 50 per tick across paid + free to start). armed_families = which family may APPLY on the unattended tick, and from when (credit-verify-outbound.sh read_arming: present = only a family's own row arms it). uvn-new-rows rows added 2026-11-14 (ask-never-asked-r1, firstmate 22:48Z): the follow-up ask to a user we already asked, about owed requests no ask named. 5 users per tick across paid + free together (NR_CAP in the tick, tick_cap here can only lower it), daily_cap 120 = 24 hourly ticks x 5. The cap is low on purpose: the family has never sent, and it rises only by a PR that cites the first runs. Every body needs its own signed copy verdict (policies/outbound-copy-enforce.json). claim-status row added 2026-11-15 (claim-status-arm-policy-r1, captain's intent in that brief): the family is in the claim group with daily_cap 500/500 and had NO armed_families row, so from the day this key reached node-8 it checked every tick and applied on none (tick.log: `claim-status-paid: DRY-RUN tick (no send): arming=policy claim-status=not armed`; last send 2026-11-07T04:30:32Z). Its unsigned_from is the date the code already carries for it (credit-verify-outbound.sh UNSIGNED_FROM[claim-status], the first send of its read-back batch): a row with no date would clear that date and leave the family armed and SIGNED-only, which sends nothing either. No cap is added or raised: both claim families together stay under shared_daily_cap.claim (25 a day at the time; raised to 200 on 2026-11-16, see the last paragraph). A family listed in a group has an armed_families row or is named, with its reason, in the test that reads this file (scripts/tests/credit-verify-outbound.bats, `every grouped family`). uvn-status:c2 row carried the same day from node-8, NOT a decision of that change: the live copy (sha256 5e66b6469e5be6dd50b39a7554a14e14cbd03f88a0608b1eb5c028d225e9fefe, mtime 2026-11-15T08:19Z, read 12:0xZ) held it and this file did not, and with the marker above a deploy of this file would have removed it and stopped the /c2 corrected asks. Every other key of the two copies was equal. tick_cap.proof-need-ask free raised 5 -> 50, the paid value, on 2026-11-14 (ask-never-asked-r1, firstmate 21:19Z): this is the one cap this file raises, and it supersedes both the 'free: 5' and the 'Nothing is raised' of the 2026-11-13 paragraph above. At 5 the free cursor moved about 6 list entries a tick while the list grew as fast, so most free users never reached the gate. The cap bounds users handed to the gate, not asks delivered; the daily cap (400) is unchanged. Caps raised 2026-11-16 (verif-caps-arm-c1; captain's intent: "nothing waiting on us", "make real verifiable progress", "PRs and CI/CD all the way through to measurable results"; the Fable verification scout's ranked table, data/verif-queue-fable-scout-f5/report.md, measured both as reversible and needing no decision): (1) shared_daily_cap.claim 25 -> 200, so the claim lane can actually use the claim-status row #2026 added - 1,411 of 1,899 claims on the list route to the claim-status note, which had sent nothing since 2026-11-07T04:30:32Z. That raise is the DAY ceiling, not a per-tick one: a family the tick holds no FULL_CAP_FROM date for is clamped per segment per tick by family_cap (FIRST_CAP, 100), so a tick hands claim-status 100 on each segment (was min(FIRST_CAP, shared 25) = 25) and the 200 bounds the two claim families together for the day. It stays inside m2's 500-a-day claim ceiling (H-DevOps k8s/prod/messaging/78-send-gateway.yaml WARMUP_CEILINGS notify 3,000, allocated credit 2,500 / claim 500) on purpose: firstmate 2026-11-16T09:51Z ruled 200 now - Fable's step, because the per-person daily gate is not live yet - and 500 only in a follow-up PR once per-user-daily-gate-r1 is deployed and one day at 200 shows no complaint or unsubscribe spike. Raising the per-tick binder is a separate change: it means dating that family. (2) tick_cap.uvn-status.free 50 -> 100, inside daily_cap.uvn-status.free 2000 (24 hourly ticks x 100 = 2,400, so the daily row is the binding cap, not the tick row). The 50 was set 2026-11-04 because the free uvn-status apply lost its outcomes artefact when the Intercom-note step hit the subprocess timeout at ~55-60 min / ~80 users (#1756); that is no longer what bounds a run: [key=note-step-budget] makes the send loop refuse to START a user whose worst case does not fit the share the tick hands it (--apply-budget-s), and a budget-deferred user waits for the next tick, so a larger cap sends more and defers the rest instead of losing the artefact. Nothing else moves: no daily_cap row, no armed_families row, no copy gate (policies/outbound-copy-enforce.json), no sender, no stop rule. Both values are pinned by scripts/tests/credit-verify-outbound.bats, in `outbound tick (verif-caps-arm-c1): the shipped policy raises the shared claim day cap to 200 and the free uvn-status tick cap to 100, and the tick hands both to the runner` and the assertions updated in `every grouped family`. Reviewed against the live copy before deploying (firstmate 2026-11-16T02:44Z): node-8 (40.160.32.80) holds /opt/hydra/policies/credit-verify-outbound.json at sha256 8757856624b07cf8c0d862b5362d0bd372f769e205ac8833916dc9b4f1522229, mtime 2026-11-16T01:39:22Z, 8075 bytes, read 2026-11-16T01:39Z and again 02:47Z (the same sha256 both times). Leaf-by-leaf it differs from this file in exactly three places: this _doc text, shared_daily_cap.claim (live 25, here 200) and tick_cap["uvn-status"].free (live 50, here 100). Nothing live-only is being dropped: there is NO watchdog hard stop to keep or clear (live tick_cap["uvn-status"] is {free: 50, paid: 50}, not 0/0), no tick_cap row exists live that this file lacks, and armed_families has the same nine keys live as here, claim-status included ({live: true, paid: true, unsigned_from: 2026-10-31T17:55Z}, carried to node-8 by #2026's deploy). The deploy therefore lifts only the two caps this change raises and changes no other value node-8 runs.

tick_cap._doc: Per-family per-tick cap. A family+segment listed here may ACCEPT at most this many users in ONE tick, whatever its daily row, its FIRST_CAP line or the global CVO_CAP says. The clamp only ever LOWERS a cap - a value above the family's own cap changes nothing, so this key can never widen a blast radius. Absent family/segment = exactly the behavior before this key existed. Added 2026-11-04 on the Fable driver's ruling: the free uvn-status apply sends until its Intercom-note step hits the subprocess timeout at ~55-60 min / ~80 users and then loses its outcomes artefact entirely (#1756, twice in one afternoon: 39 sends at 15:05Z, 79 at 17:24Z). A per-FAMILY cap was needed rather than CVO_CAP because that knob is ONE global value: setting it to 60 would also have narrowed r1, claim-status and the approved 70-send claim install.
